evidence: save(order) only calls this.orders.set(order.id, order). This is plain persistence.
findById(id) returns this.orders.get(id) || null. This is a plain lookup.
findByState(state) filters on order.getState() === state. This is a query predicate, not a business rule.
The class implements OrderRepository, the port defined in src/domain/Repository.ts (the IMPLEMENTS edge in the graph). This is the usual adapter pattern for the infrastructure layer.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: src/infrastructure/InMemoryOrderRepository.ts is a persistence adapter. It implements the domain-declared OrderRepository port and only stores and retrieves data: save, findById, findByState and all, all backed by a Map. That is the expected role for an infrastructure file. findByState filters orders by state, which is a query criterion and not a business rule. It does not decide any state transitions, validation or pricing. The file has no transport, presentation or domain decision logic.
